title: Proposition
body_md: $\Psi$ is a diffeomorphism  from $\mathcal{C}_{\theta}$ to $\mathcal{D}_{\theta}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From \eqref{Cahn-Hoffman}, we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
    F_{\theta}(\Psi(\xi))=F_{\theta} \left(\frac{\xi-\cos\theta e}{F_{\theta}(\xi-\cos\theta e)} \right)=1,
\end{eqnarray*}
and for $\xi=(\xi',0)\in \partial {\mathcal C}_\theta$, there holds
$$
\Psi (\xi) =\ell^{-1}(\xi) (\xi -\cos \theta e)=\sin^{-2}\theta(\xi',\cos \theta),
$$
which implies $\Psi$ is a map from $\mathcal{C}_{\theta}$ to $\mathcal{D}_{\theta}$.

 For all $\xi\in \mathcal{C}_{\theta}$,  direct calculations yield
   $$
D\Psi (\xi)=\left (\begin{array}{cccc}
\frac{1}{\sin^{2}\theta+\cos\theta \<\xi, e\>} &\dots&  0 & \frac{\cos\theta\xi_{1}}{(\sin^{2}\theta+\cos\theta\<\xi,e\>)^{2}} \\
 \vdots & \vdots& \ddots& \vdots\\
0&  \cdots&\frac{1}{\sin^{2}\theta+\cos\theta\<\xi,e\>} & \frac{\cos\theta \xi_{n}}{(\sin^{2}\theta +\cos\theta\<\xi,e\>)^{2}} \\
0 & \cdots &0 & \frac{1}{(\sin^{2}\theta+\cos\theta\<\xi,e\>)^{2}} \\
\end{array}\right),
$$
then its Jacobi   $\det(D \Psi(\xi))=\frac{1}{\ell^{n+2}(\xi)}>0, ~\forall \xi\in \mathcal{C}_{\theta},$ therefore $\Psi$ is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism map from $\mathcal{C}_{\theta}$ to $\mathcal{D}_{\theta}$.

name: Capillary radial function

title: Definition
body_md:
Given $\widehat\Sigma\in \mathcal{K}_\theta$ and $z\in {\rm{int}}(\widehat{\partial\Sigma})$, we define its capillary polar  body with respect to $z$ by	
     
     $$ \widehat{\Sigma}^{*}_{z}\coloneqq  \left \{X+z\in  \overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}  \mid ru_{z}(\xi)\le 1 , \text{ where } X=r\xi \text{ with } \xi\in \mathcal{C}_\theta\right\}, $$ where $u_z$ is the capillary support function of $\Sigma$ with respect to $z$.
head: environment
name: Capillary polar body

title: Remark
body_md:
It can be readily observed that 
$ru_{z}(\xi)\le 1$ is equivalent to   
\begin{eqnarray*}
r{\<\xi-\cos\theta e,y-z\>} \le \ell(\xi) \quad \forall~ y\in \Sigma.
\end{eqnarray*} 
In other words, \begin{eqnarray*}                                       
    r\<\Psi(\xi),y-z\>\leq 1~~~\forall ~ y\in \Sigma,
\end{eqnarray*} where $\Psi$ is given by \eqref{Cahn-Hoffman}. In particular, we observe that the capillary polar body of $\widehat\mathcal{C}_\theta$ (w.r.t the origin $o$)  satisfies $(\widehat{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}})^{\ast}_{o}=\widehat{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}}$.

body_md:
Given $\widehat\Sigma\in \mathcal{K}_\theta$ with $\theta\in(0, \pi/2)$, if there exists a  point $z_{s}=z_s(\widehat\Sigma) \in \widehat{\partial\Sigma}$ such that  
$${\rm{Vol}}(\widehat{\Sigma}^*_{z_s})= \inf_{z\in {\rm{int}}(\widehat{\partial \Sigma})} {\rm{Vol}}(\widehat{\Sigma}_z^*),$$ then we call $z_s$ the capillary Santal\'o point of $\widehat{\Sigma}$.
head: environment
name: Capillary Santal\'o point

label: pro-santalo
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: L-contained
title: Proof
body_md:
First, we show that the capillary Santal\'o point $z_{s}$ lies in ${\rm{int}}(\widehat{\partial\Sigma})$. We argue by contradiction and assume that $z_{s} \in \partial \Sigma \cap \partial  {\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. Without loss of generality,  assume $z_{s}$ is the origin. Since $\widehat{\partial \Sigma}$ is a closed convex body in $\partial {\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}} = \mathbb{R}^n$, it follows from \cite[Proof of Lemma~2.2, claim (2.3)]{GN} that there exists a unit vector $\zeta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (specifically, $\zeta$ is the unit outward normal of $\partial \Sigma \subset \widehat{\partial \Sigma}$ at the origin, and for notational convenience, we may assume $\zeta = E_1$,) such that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{L-contained}
L \coloneqq \left\{ -t E_1 \mid  0 < t < t_{0} \right\}\text{ is contained in }\widehat{\partial \Sigma},~\text{ for some small } t_{0}>0.
\end{eqnarray}
Moreover, due to $\theta \in (0,\pi/2)$, the set $\widehat{\Sigma}$ is contained in the half-space $\{x_{1}\leq 0\}$ and is tangent to the hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$ at the origin. 

For $\xi\coloneqq (\xi_{1}, \xi_{2},\cdots, \xi_{n+1})\in \mathcal{C}_{\theta}$,  define $N(\xi)\coloneqq(-\xi_{1}, \xi_{2}, \cdots, \xi_{n+1})$.
Since $$u_{z_s}(\xi)=\ell^{-1}(\xi)\sup\limits_{X\in \Sigma}\<X, \xi+\cos\theta E_{n+1}\>,$$ for all $\xi\in \mathcal{C}_\theta$, then
 there exists a point $z(\xi)\in \Sigma$, such that 
 $$u_{z_s}(\xi)=\ell^{-1}(\xi)\<z(\xi), \xi+\cos\theta E_{n+1}\>.$$
For all $\xi\in \mathcal{C}_{\theta}$ with $\xi_{1}\geq 0$, by the Definition  \ref{defn-capillary-support}, we have
\begin{eqnarray}
    u_{z_s}\left(N(\xi)\right)&\geq &\ell^{-1}(N(\xi))\<z(\xi), N(\xi)+\cos\theta E_{n+1}\>\notag                                                                 
    \\
    &=& \ell^{-1}(\xi)\<z(\xi), \xi+\cos\theta E_{n+1}\>-\ell^{-1}(\xi)\< z(\xi), 2 E_1 \>\notag
    \\
    &\geq& \ell^{-1}(\xi)\<z(\xi), \xi+\cos\theta E_{n+1}\>=u_{z_{s}}(\xi), \label{big}
\end{eqnarray}
where the last line used the fact that  $\<z(\xi), E_1\> \le 0$. Moreover, the above inequality is strict for a subset of $\xi \in \mathcal{C}_{\theta}$ of positive measure.

Consider the function  $$u_{z_t}(\xi)\coloneqq u_{z_s}(\xi)+t\frac{\xi_1}{\ell (\xi)}, ~~~\xi\in \mathcal{C}_\theta, ~~t\in(0, t_0). $$ 
From Definition \ref{defn-capillary-support}, we know that $u_{z_t}$ is the capillary support function of $\widehat{\Sigma}$ with respect to the point $z_{t}=-tE_1$ for all  $0<t<t_{0}$. From \eqref{L-contained}, we have $u_{z_t}(\xi)>0$ for all $t\in(0, t_0)$.  
Using Proposition \ref{prop-volume-polar-body} and \eqref{big}, we compute
\begin{eqnarray*}
    0&\leq& \frac{d}{dt}\left({\rm{Vol}}(\widehat{\Sigma}^{\ast}_{z_{t}})\right)\Big|_{t=0}=-\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}}\frac{\xi_{1}}{u_{z_{s}}^{n+2}(\xi)}d\sigma\\
    &=&-\left(\int_{\{\xi_{1}>0\}}\frac{\xi_{1}}{u_{z_{s}}^{n+2}(\xi)}d\sigma+\int_{\{\xi_{1}<0\}}\frac{\xi_{ 1}}{u_{z_{s}}^{n+2}(\xi)}d\sigma\right)\\
    &=&-\left(\int_{\{\xi_{1}>0\}}\left(\frac{ \xi_{1}}{u_{z_s}^{n+2}(\xi)}-\frac{ \xi_{1} }{u_{z_s}^{n+2}(N(\xi))}\right)d\sigma\right)<0,
\end{eqnarray*}
this reaches a contradiction. Hence we get $z_{s}\in   \rm{int}(\widehat{\partial \Sigma})$.                        

Next, we move on to prove \eqref{santalo-point-ortho}. 
Let $z_s^{\varepsilon,i} \coloneqq z_{s}+\varepsilon E_{i}$ with $1\leq i\leq n$. For some sufficiently small $\varepsilon_0 > 0$, we have $$z_s^{\varepsilon,i} \in {\rm{int}}(\widehat{\partial\Sigma}) ~~\text{ for all } |\varepsilon| \leq \varepsilon_0,$$ together with Proposition~\ref{prop-volume-polar-body}, we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
   0= \frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\left({\rm{Vol}}(\widehat{\Sigma}^{\ast}_{z_s^{\varepsilon,i}})\right)\Big|_{\varepsilon=0} =\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}}\frac{\xi_{i}}{u_{z_{s}}^{n+2}(\xi)}d\sigma, ~~\text{ for all }~~1\leq i\leq n.
\end{eqnarray*} Hence the assertion \eqref{santalo-point-ortho} follows.  

Finally, we prove the uniqueness of the capillary Santal\'o point.  Without loss of generality,  we assume the capillary Santal\'o point $z_s$ is the origin and it lies in ${\rm{int}}(\widehat{\partial\Sigma})$ by the preceding argument. For all $z\in \widehat{\partial\Sigma}$, we rewrite $z\coloneqq (z_1,\cdots, z_n,0)$, and                                                            
\begin{eqnarray}\label{uz}
        u_{z}(\xi)=u(\xi)-  \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} \frac{z_{i}\xi_{i}}{\ell(\xi)} , \quad \xi\in \mathcal{C}_{\theta},
\end{eqnarray}where $u$ is the capillary support function of $\Sigma$ with respect to the origin. Inserting \eqref{uz} into \eqref{vol} implies
\begin{eqnarray*}
 {\rm{Vol}}(\widehat{\Sigma}_{z}^{\ast})=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}}\frac{\ell(\xi)}{\left(u(\xi)-\ell^{-1}(\xi)\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}z_{i}\xi_{i}\right)^{n+1}}d\sigma\eqqcolon V(z).
\end{eqnarray*}
A direct calculation shows that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
    \frac{\partial^{2}V(z)}{\partial z_{i}\partial z_{j}}=(n+2)\int_{\mathcal{C}_{\theta}}\frac{\xi_{i}\xi_{j}}{\ell(\xi)u_{z}^{n+3}(\xi)}d\sigma, ~~~\text{ for all } 1\leq i, j \leq n.
\end{eqnarray*} This implies the strict convexity of the function $V(z)$ with respect to $z\in\widehat{\partial\Sigma}$, which in turn yields the uniqueness of the capillary Santal\'o point. This completes the proof.

title: Proposition
body_md: Let $\Sigma_0$ be a strictly convex capillary hypersurface in $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$ with $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$, then capillary hypersurface $\Sigma_t$ of flow  \eqref{c-Gauss curvature flow} exists for a finite time $T^*<\infty$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Without loss of generality, we assume that the origin lies in the interior of $\text{int}(\widehat{\partial{\Sigma_0}})$. Then there exists some $r_0>0$ such that $\Sigma_0\subset \widehat{\mathcal{C}_{r_{0}, \theta}}$. Define $$r(t)\coloneqq \left[ r_0^{ n+1}- ( n+1)t \right] ^{\frac{1}{ n+1}},$$ we find that  $ {\mathcal{C}_{r(t), \theta}}$ is a solution to flow \eqref{c-Gauss curvature flow} starting from $\Sigma_{0}=\mathcal{C}_{r_{0}, \theta}$.
By the comparison principle (see, e.g., \cite[Proposition 4.2]{WW20}), we know that $\Sigma_t\subset \widehat{\mathcal{C}_{r(t), \theta}}$.
It is obvious that $r(t)$ converges to zero at a finite time as $t\nearrow \frac{r_0^{n+1}}{n+1}$. Therefore, $\Sigma_t$ cannot exist beyond that time.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let  $\widehat{\Sigma}_t$ denote the convex domain enclosed in $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$ by $\Sigma_t$ and $\partial\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$. Since $\Sigma_t$ is the solution of flow \eqref{c-Gauss curvature flow}, 
by the comparison principle   we know that $\widehat{\Sigma}_t\subset \widehat{\Sigma}_s$, for any $s<t$. 
 
First, we demonstrate that the capillary inner radius $\rho_{-}(\widehat\Sigma_t ,\theta)$ of $\Sigma_t$ tends to zero as $t\rightarrow T^{\ast}$. In fact, if this is not true, since the flow is a contracting flow and by the definition of $\rho_-(\widehat\Sigma_t,\theta)$, we know that there exists a spherical cap with some radius $r_{0}>0$ which is contained in $\Sigma_{t}$ for $ t\in [0, T^{\ast})$. Combining Proposition \ref{curvature est} and
  the standard parabolic equation theory (see, e.g., \cite[Theorem 6.1, Theorem 6.4 and Theorem 6.5]{Dong}, and also \cite[Theorem 14.23]{Lieberman-book-parabolic}), we obtain a uniform $C^{k,\alpha}$ estimate of the solution to flow \eqref{support fun eq. of capillary alpha-GCF} for all $k\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$. Therefore, flow \eqref{support fun eq. of capillary alpha-GCF} can be extended up to time $T^*+\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, which contradicts the fact that $T^*<+\infty$ is the maximal existence time of flow \eqref{support fun eq. of capillary alpha-GCF}. 


Next, we prove that as $t\rightarrow T^{\ast}$, the hypersurface $\Sigma_{t}$ converges to a point. Suppose, by contradiction, that $\cap_{t\geq 0}\widehat{\Sigma}_{t}$ is not a point. Let $\text{diam}(\cap_{t\geq 0}\widehat{\Sigma}_{t})=l_{0}=\text{dist}(x_{1}, x_{2})$  where $x_{1}, x_{2}\in \cap_{t\geq 0}\widehat{\Sigma}_{t}$. 
Since the inner capillary radius tends to zero, the volume of $\widehat{\Sigma}_{t}$  also converges to zero. Thus, there exists a two dimension hyperplane $\mathcal{H}$ such that the area of $\bar{H}\coloneqq \mathcal{H}\cap \left(\cap_{t\geq 0}\widehat{\Sigma}_{t}\right)$  converges to zero.  Along the boundary of $\bar{H}\cap \partial (\cap_{t\geq 0}\widehat{\Sigma}_{t})$, there must be some point with arbitrarily small principal curvature. However, Proposition \ref{curvature est} implies the principal curvatures of $\Sigma_{t}$  have a uniformly lower bound. Thus, we derive a contradiction, and  $\widehat{\Sigma}_{t}$ converges to a point as $t\rightarrow T^{\ast}$.

label: soliton-alpha-GCF
title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $\Sigma_0$ be a strictly convex capillary hypersurface in $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$ and $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$. If $\alpha>0$, then the flow \eqref{cap-alpha-Gauss curvature flow} has a smooth solution $\Sigma_t\coloneqq X(M,t)$, which is strictly convex capillary hypersurface for all $t\in[0, T^*)$, where $T^*\coloneqq \frac 1 {\alpha n+1}\left(\frac{{\rm{Vol}}(\widehat\Sigma_0)}{{\rm{Vol}}(\widehat\mathcal{C}_{\theta})} \right)^{\frac{\alpha n+1}{n+1}}$. As $t\to T^*$, then the capillary hypersurfaces $\Sigma_t$ shrink to a point $p\in \partial{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$.
 Moreover,  if $\alpha>\frac 1{n+2}$, the solution of normalized flow \eqref{c-alpha-GCF-capillary-normalized} converges to a smooth, strictly convex capillary hypersurface $\Sigma_\infty\subset \overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+}$ as  $t\to +\infty$.                                                                                    
 Furthermore, $\Sigma_\infty$ satisfies: \begin{eqnarray}\label{soliton-alpha-GCF}\left\{
\begin{array}{llll}
	K^\alpha  &=& \lambda \frac{\<X,\nu\> } {1+\cos\theta\<\nu, e\>} & \text{  in } ~~ \Sigma_\infty,\\ 
	\<\nu,e\>&=& -\cos\theta & \text{ on }~~ \partial \Sigma_\infty,\end{array} \right.
\end{eqnarray} where $\lambda\coloneqq \frac {1}{(n+1) {\rm{Vol}}(\widehat\mathcal{C}_\theta)} \int_{\mathcal{C}_\theta} K^{\alpha-1}(\xi) \left(\sin^2\theta+\cos\theta\<\xi,e\>\right) d\xi$.
